source.note: The authoritative product story. Where an older product document disagrees with this deck, this deck wins.

positioning.headline: An intelligent credit investigation layer for risk teams.
positioning.tagline: From risk signals to risk action.
positioning.distinction: It does not answer questions about the credit book. It investigates it.

arc_questions.Decide: What should we do about it?
arc_questions.Drive Alignment: How do we align everyone around it?

positioning.plain_arc: See the risk → understand the why → choose the response → mobilise the action
positioning.arc_note: A shared operating story across modules, not a rule assigning one module per stage.

audience.the_real_problem: The difficulty is rarely a shortage of information. It is that the evidence is fragmented, and connecting it takes longer than the decision allows.
consequences: too much time goes into assembling evidence rather than judging it
signal is hard to separate from noise
portfolio and borrower evidence sit apart
emerging risk is disconnected from structural credit quality
stress work is disconnected from current deterioration
committee packs are assembled by hand
actions and owners drift away from the evidence behind them
dependencies and overdue work hide across plans and meetings
questions_a_cro_asks: What happens under a downside scenario?

modules.name: Cockpit
modules.one_line: Interrogate the recorded credit book: what moved, why, and who to look at next.
modules.why_it_matters: A senior credit officer can see that ECL moved without being able to say what moved it, which borrowers are behind it, or which of them is worth a review this week.
modules.how_it_works: Cockpit classifies the question, chooses the execution path it needs, and explains the evidence it gets back. Four question types: a definition and product help answer directly; a data operation runs SQL; an analysis runs SQL and Python together.

question_types.example: How do I run a What-If scenario?

worked_example.question: Decompose the ECL movement for me.
worked_example.scope: Corporate portfolio Q1 → Q2 2026, SAR million
worked_example.what_changed: ECL rose from SAR 240m to SAR 300m — up SAR 60m, or 25%. Exposure grew 4.2% while ECL coverage moved from 2.0% to 2.4%.
worked_example.what_explains_it: A sequential revaluation bridge — not an independently validated attribution method. Construction contributes 60% of the increase.
what_next: prioritise the construction borrowers contributing most to the movement
review stage, rating and collateral evidence for those borrowers
run the targeted construction downside scenario and prepare committee review
worked_example.label: deck example, not live data

modules.owns: historical and recorded corporate credit analysis, product help, and stable credit and accounting concepts
modules.does_not_own: emerging deterioration workflow (Early Warning), prospective shocks (What-If), model validation (Scorecard Validation), committee packs (Playbook), dashboards (Lenses), delivery plans (AI Project Planner)
modules.boundary: Cockpit explains the evidence it retrieved. It does not invent the underlying financial calculation.
example_questions: What is total exposure at default by sector in the latest quarter?
Which sectors saw the largest increase in Stage 2 exposure over the latest year?
Decompose the ECL movement between the last two quarters.
Which borrowers contribute most to the construction ECL increase?

modules.name: Early Warning Analysis
modules.one_line: Identify emerging deterioration early, size how serious it is, and escalate it to an owner.
modules.why_it_matters: Deterioration usually shows up in behaviour before it shows up in a rating. The difficulty is telling one weak signal apart from several worsening together, and knowing which borrower can least afford it.
modules.core_principle: Fresh signals drive the warning. Structural credit quality determines how seriously they are interpreted.

tac.summary: TAC turns live behaviour into a context-aware risk signal. It is applied across all four intelligence layers.

T.name: Trigger
T.question: What changed?
T.detail: A change-based deviation from the customer's own normal, drawn from high-frequency data — not a static threshold.

A.name: Accelerator
A.question: How fast, how convincingly?
A.detail: Weighs the shape of the deterioration, not merely its presence. One weak signal is not several worsening together.

C.name: Classifier
C.question: Who is it happening to?
C.detail: Slow-moving structural quality, reviewed periodically rather than re-scored daily. The same behaviour is read differently in a vulnerable borrower.

tac.scoring: Conceptual and configurable: the TAC-adjusted signal is approximately trigger × acceleration × classifier.
tac.same_behaviour_different_risk: A 30% decline in operating or deposit balance is a WATCH for a borrower with a strong rating and comfortable DSCR, and a HIGH CONCERN for one with a weak rating and thin DSCR. Classifiers change the interpretation, not the underlying observation.

layers.summary: Four intelligence layers feed one TAC-based engine. Every alert names its layer, its driver and its evidence.

items.name: Internal behavioural intelligence
items.question: What is changing inside the banking relationship?
items.note: Detects live deterioration — the usual source of fresh triggers.

items.name: Credit and financial fundamentals
items.question: Who is the customer, and how vulnerable are they?
items.note: Structural credit quality calibrates severity — periodic, not daily.

items.name: External intelligence
items.question: What is happening outside the bank's own data?
items.note: Converts external events into traceable borrower-level signals.
pipeline: entity resolution — is this actually my borrower?
event extraction — structured, not a keyword hit
relevance and materiality — does it move cash flow or repayment?

items.name: Graph and relationship intelligence
items.question: Where can risk travel from?
items.note: Sees risk around the borrower, not only inside it.

worked_example.summary: Cedar Infrastructure moved from 68 to 88 — CRITICAL — as four independent layers deteriorated together: a fresh Layer 1 cash-flow signal, a Layer 2 context that was already weak, a Layer 3 disclosed contract delay corroborating the internal signal, and a Layer 4 dependency on a supplier now in confirmed distress. The combination, not any single signal, drives the severity.
worked_example.label: deck example, not live data

modules.boundary: Escalation and limit changes are proposals routed through the configured escalation matrix and approved by the bank — not decided autonomously. Early detection is not guaranteed.
modules.owns: emerging deterioration and the warning and escalation workflow
example_questions: What is TAC?
What are the four Early Warning intelligence layers?
Why is a borrower flagged High rather than Watch?
Which customers moved into Critical since the last run?

modules.name: What-If Analysis
modules.one_line: Test a prospective shock and see what it would do to the portfolio.
modules.why_it_matters: Knowing a sector is deteriorating is not the same as knowing what a further downgrade or a fall in collateral values would cost, or whether the scenario is plausible enough to act on.
modules.how_it_works: A scenario is defined explicitly — scope, baseline, shocks and horizon — and the impact is computed from configured rating mappings and collateral assumptions.

worked_example.request: Simulate a one-notch downgrade for construction borrowers and a 20% fall in their property collateral values. What is the portfolio impact, and how likely is this over the next 12 months?
worked_example.scenario: Scope construction, baseline Q2 2026, one-notch rating shock, −20% collateral, 12-month horizon
worked_example.impact: Portfolio ECL +SAR 80m (+26.7%); ECL/EAD 2.40% → 3.04%. Rating/PD +40, collateral/LGD +25, interaction +15, not double-counted. EAD unchanged; other sectors held flat as a simplifying assumption.
worked_example.likelihood: Plausible as an adverse stress if migration and collateral-market evidence support it. A probability is not quantified from these inputs alone.
worked_example.label: deck example, not live data

modules.boundary: The scenario horizon is distinct from the applicable ECL measurement horizon. Outputs follow configured mappings and assumptions — they are not automatic consequences of the shocks alone, and not every downgrade moves a borrower into Stage 2. A probability is not asserted without evidence.
modules.owns: prospective and hypothetical shocks and scenarios
example_questions: What happens if construction borrowers are downgraded one notch?
What is the ECL impact of a 20% fall in property collateral?
How does the stressed case compare with baseline?

modules.name: Scorecard Validation
modules.one_line: Assess whether a scorecard is still working, and diagnose what is wrong when it is not.
modules.why_it_matters: A model-risk leader needs to know not only that discrimination has weakened but which variable is behaving against expectation, and to produce validation evidence a reviewer will accept.

worked_example.question: What is the issue with my scorecard?
worked_example.finding: Discrimination is weak: KS = 22, below the internal benchmark of 30. KS is a 22-percentage-point maximum separation between cumulative default and non-default distributions — not an accuracy of 22%. The benchmark is a demo assumption, not a universal regulatory threshold.
worked_example.diagnosis: Debt-to-income has a counterintuitive fitted effect: higher DTI is reducing predicted default risk, the opposite of the stated business expectation.
worked_example.label: deck example, not live data

modules.boundary: A low aggregate metric does not prove which variable caused it. Coding, binning, missing-value treatment and sign conventions are checked first, and removing a variable is not guaranteed to improve the metric. Reviewers approve any model change.
example_questions: What is the issue with my scorecard?
Is the model still discriminating well?
Which variables behave against expectation?

modules.name: Playbook
modules.one_line: Turn analyses and evidence into a committee-ready narrative with the decisions named.
modules.why_it_matters: Committee packs are assembled by hand, and the claims in them drift away from the analysis that produced them.
produces: a draft narrative following the prior pack's structure
material claims linked to numbered evidence

decision_questions: Which deteriorating borrowers require committee escalation?
Should a targeted limit and collateral review be approved?
What further evidence is needed before agreeing the response?
worked_example.label: deck example, not live data

modules.boundary: Playbook organises supplied material, drafts the narrative, links evidence and extracts questions. It does not invent committee approval.
modules.owns: committee narrative, evidence linkage and decision questions
example_questions: Develop a committee report for me.
What decision questions come out of this quarter's analysis?
Link the ECL movement to the evidence behind it.

modules.name: Lenses
modules.one_line: Bring the indicators an executive actually watches onto one screen.
modules.why_it_matters: A CRO wants the movement and the reason on the same screen, not a dashboard that shows a number and leaves the explanation somewhere else.
produces: a short written read of what moved
modules.boundary: Metrics are brought together from relevant CreditProbe datasets, not unrestricted access to every possible source. 'Last refreshed' reflects when the screen re-rendered, not that source observations changed. Stage 3 exposure is shown as defined, not relabelled as NPL.
example_questions: Create a CRO dashboard.
How has ECL coverage moved this quarter?

modules.name: AI Project Planner
modules.one_line: Keep risk and model-risk workstreams moving by tracking dependencies, blockers and overdue work.
modules.why_it_matters: Risk and model-risk initiatives fail quietly: a review goes overdue, a sign-off blocks everything downstream, owners are fragmented and the delivery risk is invisible until the deadline.
monitoring_flow: due now → request update or confirm evidence
missed or blocked → notify and escalate per policy

worked_example.summary: In an eight-week scorecard validation and remediation plan, independent review is overdue, which directly blocks methodology sign-off and puts remediation at risk.
worked_example.label: deck example, not live data

modules.boundary: Users approve material changes to ownership, dates and the plan. A product demonstration is not evidence that a real notification was sent.
example_questions: What is blocking the validation plan?
Which milestones are overdue?
Who needs to be notified about the delay?

supporting_capabilities.name: Data Builder
supporting_capabilities.one_line: Cross-domain evidence: assemble the data an investigation needs from across the domains that hold it.

supporting_capabilities.name: Graph Data
supporting_capabilities.one_line: Relationship intelligence: parents, guarantors, suppliers, customers and the paths risk can travel along.

supporting_capabilities.name: Borrower 360
supporting_capabilities.one_line: Complete credit context for one borrower in one place.

supporting_capabilities.name: Root-Cause Investigation
supporting_capabilities.one_line: From signal to why: work a movement back to what caused it.

supporting_capabilities.name: Action Matrix
supporting_capabilities.one_line: Define the response: what should happen, to whom, by when.

supporting_capabilities.name: Escalation Matrix
supporting_capabilities.one_line: Escalate with purpose, through the configured policy rather than ad hoc.

supporting_capabilities.name: Transportable Investigation
supporting_capabilities.one_line: Take the evidence with you into the meeting it is needed in.

supporting_capabilities.name: Workflow
supporting_capabilities.one_line: Notify, assign and align the people who have to act.

supporting_capabilities.name: Agentic AI Portfolio Watchdog
supporting_capabilities.one_line: Watches the portfolio for movement worth a person's attention.

relationships.difference: Cockpit explains what the recorded book already shows — what moved and why. Early Warning looks forward from live behaviour to borrowers that are starting to deteriorate.
relationships.together: Cockpit identifies that construction ECL moved and which borrowers sit behind it; Early Warning says which of those borrowers are deteriorating now and on what evidence.

relationships.difference: Cockpit is historical and recorded: it analyses what the book actually shows. What-If is prospective: it applies a shock that has not happened and computes the consequence.
relationships.together: Cockpit sizes the movement that already happened; What-If tests what a further downgrade or collateral fall would add.

relationships.difference: Early Warning is about deterioration that is already visible in behaviour and evidence. What-If is about a hypothetical shock and its modelled impact.
relationships.together: Early Warning names the borrowers under pressure; What-If tests how much worse a plausible adverse scenario would make them.
Cockpit establishes the movement and its drivers, What-If tests the adverse case, and Playbook turns both into a committee narrative with the decisions named and the evidence linked.
Early Warning produces ranked deteriorating borrowers with layer-tagged drivers and an evidence trail; Playbook carries that evidence into the committee story and extracts the decisions it implies.
Scorecard Validation produces findings and a remediation plan; Planner tracks the workstream, its dependencies and what is blocking sign-off.

relationships.difference: Lenses is a standing view of the indicators an executive watches. Cockpit is where a question about one of them gets investigated.

never_claim: unrestricted access to every possible data source
governance: Human accountability and approval remain explicit.
Limit changes are proposals subject to the bank's approval, escalated through the configured escalation matrix rather than decided autonomously. (slide 8)
Playbook organises material and drafts narrative; it does not invent committee approval. (slide 11)
Users approve material changes to ownership, dates and the plan. (slide 13)
Cockpit explains returned evidence; it does not invent the underlying financial calculation. (slide 4)
boundaries.demo_data: This environment uses synthetic demonstration data, not a real bank portfolio. Figures in the product deck are illustrative examples of the product, never current portfolio values.

historical_architecture.label: NOT_CURRENT_V4_ARCHITECTURE
historical_architecture.summary: Slide 14 of the deck describes an earlier Cockpit request lifecycle: two Sonnet/Qwen preprocessing passes, a separate ownership-gate call, a separate analysis-plan call, a sufficiency-review call, a separate final-answer call, an answer-rewrite and a thread-summary call after delivery.
historical_architecture.why_excluded: The current Cockpit V4 runtime is a single continuing Opus analyst with governed tools. It has no Sonnet preprocessing, no separate ownership-gate call, no planning essay, no mandatory separate final-answer call and no summary-before-answer step. This section is retained for provenance only and must never be described as how the product works today.
